generatedCommentsNodes.comment: The `bulkItemResponses` helper interleaves `id.get()` (in the second `.map`) with `id.getAndIncrement()` (in the `toMap` key function) inside a single stream pipeline. This works correctly for sequential streams because each element fully traverses the pipeline before the next begins, but it is fragile and hard to verify at a glance. A simple indexed loop or `IntStream.range` would make the ID assignment unambiguous and avoid relying on stream evaluation order for a side-effecting counter.

The `doProcessCount` field is a plain `int` that is read and decremented in `doProcess` without synchronization. While the test flow is sequential in practice, `doProcess` is a method on a shared object and could theoretically be invoked from different threads (e.g., if the async job mechanism dispatches work on a different thread). Using `AtomicInteger` with `decrementAndGet()` / `get()` would make the intent and safety explicit, and the cost is negligible in a test.

The two sites use different mechanisms to detect `IndexNotFoundException`:
- `#5P3ME` checks `IndexNotFoundException.class.isAssignableFrom(cause.getClass())` on the *direct* cause of the bulk item failure.
- `#YBR2R` checks `elasticsearchException instanceof IndexNotFoundException` on an already-unwrapped throwable.
Both are correct for the typical Elasticsearch bulk-failure shape (where the cause is the exception itself). However, if a future change wraps `IndexNotFoundException` inside another `ElasticsearchException` (e.g., a `ShardSearchFailure` or a custom wrapper), the `instanceof` check in `#YBR2R` would miss it while the `isAssignableFrom` check in `#5P3ME` would also miss it (since it only inspects the immediate cause class). Consider whether a small helper that walks the cause chain (similar to the existing `unwrappedThrowable` logic) should be shared between both call sites to keep the detection consistent.

If we no longer consider `IndexNotFoundException` irrecoverable, could we modify the `isExceptionIrrecoverable` method to reflect that instead of adding the `isNotIndexNotFoundException` method?

Or the distinction is still needed for cases other than bulk responses?

That is a good question - at least for now I was thinking of just handling it for the destination index? The source index can still fail with IndexNotFoundException (if PIT == null): https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/main/x-pack/plugin/transform/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/transform/transforms/ClientTransformIndexer.java#L602

I haven't seen this same type of intermittent failure scenario though, where the source index gets relocated to a new shard and the request fails on the old shard, so I'm not sure if we just haven't seen it yet or if search behaves differently where the request will automatically reroute.

> I'm not sure if we just haven't seen it yet or if search behaves differently where the request will automatically reroute.

I don't know either unfortunately :(
But since we are going in a direction to make more errors recoverable (and more transforms unattended) it could make sense to make `IndexNotFoundException` recoverable.
But maybe let's not do it in this PR if you don't feel comfortable.
We can leave this PR for dealing with destination index only.
Please make it clear in the PR title/description.
